subject: Day 6: end of week 1; weight starts climbing; insurance check
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 6. End of week 1. Weight should be turning the corner; most term infants are gaining 0.5-1 oz per day from today through day 14. Bilirubin should be trending down if physiologic. The mother is in the lochia rubra-to-serosa transition, with bleeding tapering from menstrual-heavy to lighter pink-brown. The 7-10 day weight check is the next scheduled clinical event.

Action items
- Confirm the day 7-10 weight check is on the calendar. Pediatrician will verify Avi has crossed back over toward birth weight and that latch or formula intake is sustainable. AAP Bright Futures periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Call the insurance company to verify Avi's enrollment has actually processed. The form is not the same as enrollment. Insurance companies do not retroactively cover well visits if the enrollment lapsed. Healthcare.gov reference on QLEs: https://www.healthcare.gov/glossary/qualifying-life-event/
- If the SS-5 has been mailed and Avi's Social Security card has not arrived, expect it any day from now through week 3. SSA SSN application status: https://www.ssa.gov/ssnumber/
- Establish a night-shift split if both parents are still home. The 11pm-3am / 3am-7am rotation outperforms both-parents-up-for-everything by a wide margin on sleep architecture and stress hormones. ACOG postpartum care overview: https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-pain-management
- Continue the feeding log into week 2.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Bilirubin trending down. Mustard-yellow or tan stool. Cord stump drying. Cluster feeding in the evening. Baby acne peaking around days 3-7.
- [low concern] Mother's bleeding lighter today than three days ago.
- [monitor] Bilirubin still climbing or yellow tinge spreading below the chest (call the pediatrician). Maternal bleeding suddenly heavier or large clots (call the OB).
- [call within 24h] Yellow tinge on legs or below. Fewer than six wet diapers in a day. Persistent inability to latch. Weight loss still progressing rather than reversing. Foul-smelling cord discharge.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusal of feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Maternal soaking-a-pad-per-hour bleeding or chest pain — call the OB or 911. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunity
Narrate one ordinary task in detail during Avi's next awake-alert window — warming a bottle, folding laundry, paying a bill. Conversational turns predict later language outcomes more reliably than raw word count. Romeo et al., Psych Science 2018 on PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/

Upcoming
- Day 7-10: weight check; most regain birth weight by day 14.
- Day 5-15: cord stump dries and detaches.
- Day 14-21: first common growth spurt.
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit window opens; first social smiles begin.
- Day 42: maternal 6-week postpartum visit (clearance for exercise and intimacy).

Further reading
- ACOG on the postpartum period (week 1-6): https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-pain-management
- AAP HealthyChildren overview of the first month: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Cribsheet by Emily Oster — evidence-based decisions: https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/562146/cribsheet-by-emily-oster/
- The Happiest Baby on the Block by Harvey Karp: https://www.happiestbaby.com/pages/dr-harvey-karp

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Moves both arms and both legs
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Symmetric, spontaneous movement of all four limbs. Asymmetry warrants pediatric attention.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-arms-and-legs/complete

- Reacts to loud sounds (startle, blink, stillness)
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Confirms intact hearing response. Universal newborn hearing screen catches most cases but daily observation matters.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/responds-to-loud-sound/complete

- Brings hands within range of eyes and mouth
  AAP window: day 0-45
  What to look for: Early body awareness. Not yet purposeful — looks like accidental discovery.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/brings-hands-near-face/complete

- Turns head side to side while on tummy
  AAP window: day 0-45
  What to look for: Protective reflex — keeps airway clear during tummy time.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/head-side-to-side-tummy/complete

- Focuses on objects 8-12 inches away
  AAP window: day 0-45
  What to look for: Natural breastfeeding distance. Newborn vision is otherwise blurry.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/focuses-near-objects/complete
